Section 11

Koala Court

Judicial Reform Package. Last year’s system was apparently too loose, too corrupt and insufficiently documented. This year’s is documented.

Clerk mode: one phone keeps the court record. Hand it to the Judge at dinner and enter each charge as it’s laid.

JudgeMelissa
Deputy MarshallMarshall
Legal statusExtremely robust if your legal system is a pub
The rules

Procedure

  • Each rider gets five points per night to allocate.
  • Participation is mandatory.
  • A person has 60 seconds to present charges.
  • The accused receives no rebuttal.
  • No appeal mechanism exists.
  • Evidence is not required. Witnesses are not required. Truth is apparently optional.
  • The Judge and Deputy Marshall may impose sanctions and grant good-behaviour reductions.

Possible offences

  • Missing a turn
  • Forgetting gear
  • Taking too long
  • Poor parking
  • Delaying a photo
  • Walking slowly
  • Existing in an annoying fashion
  • Indicator misuse
  • Overtaking-related misconduct
  • Looking too pleased with yourself

The reforms also note no meaningful connection to justice. Asked whether events had to be witnessed, the answer, in practical terms, was no.

Record a charge

Sixty seconds per charge. Not one more.

      Tour brief

      Meet

      Lanyon Shops car park, same as last year. 8:30 am coffee and catch-up, 9:00 am departure.

      Fuel rule

      Refuel at the end of each day. Longest gap between fuel stops is 183 km.

      • Day 1: Yass, Cowra, Blayney
      • Day 2: Lithgow, Picton, Shellharbour
      • Day 3: Bowral, Kiama, Huskisson
      • Day 4: Bungendore

      Beds

      • Millthorpe Motel, 26 Victoria St, Millthorpe
      • Barrack Point Holiday Park, Jason Ave, Barrack Point
      • Huskisson Beach Motel, 9 Hawke St, Huskisson

      Couples in queens, everyone else in twins. Dinners booked at all three by Gary G; see Dinners.

      Cornerman

      • Don’t overtake the nominated leader.
      • Sweep stays at the rear unless a new sweep is named.
      • Don’t turn at an intersection unless you can see the rider behind you.
      • Lost? Call Tony, then Ewart, then Gary G. Numbers are in WhatsApp.

      Tool kit

      Puncture kit with air, cable ties, Allen keys, spanners, nuts and bolts, screwdrivers, fuses, chain lube. First aid kit; confirm who is trained.

      Bike prep

      Service, tyres and pressures, chain lube, mirrors, tight bolts (especially Harleys), oil and water, brake pads, lever adjustment, charged battery, comms and nav set up.
